name: Taiwan
summary: Taiwan is a civil-law, highly codified employment regime built on the Labor Standards Act (LSA): there is no at-will employment, dismissal requires a statutory ground plus the courts' 'last resort' test, and almost every employee (including senior engineers) is covered by overtime, rest-day and minute-level attendance-record rules. 2025-26 brought a heavy change load: four extra paid public holidays (16 total), day-based parental leave and hourly family-care leave, new sick-leave anti-retaliation rules, a workplace-bullying chapter in the OSH Act (effective 1 July 2026), PDPA amendments creating an independent Personal Data Protection Commission, and a 2026 minimum wage of NT$29,500/NT$196. For chip employers, national-security overlays are unique: the National Security Act criminalizes misappropriation of listed 'national core key technologies' (including AI/HPC chip design and chiplet interconnect design), and investigators actively pursue PRC-linked talent poaching. US-HQ employers most often get wrong: treating engineers as overtime-exempt, running US-style PIP-and-terminate or at-will exits, using uncompensated non-competes, and skipping Taiwan-specific formalities (work-rule filing, labor-management meetings, 10-day layoff notification).

ratingNotes.termination: Only LSA Art. 11/12 grounds, courts apply 'last resort' and redeployment tests, invalid dismissals mean reinstatement plus back pay, and there is a 10-day government layoff notification.
ratingNotes.representation: Labor-management meetings are mandatory (quarterly) and must approve overtime and flexible-hours schemes, but unions are rare in foreign tech offices and co-determination is weak.
ratingNotes.privacy: PDPA requires notice, a purpose limit and written consent or a legal basis for sensitive data; the 2025 amendments add an independent PDPC and mandatory breach reporting (effective date pending).
ratingNotes.payTransparency: Salary ranges must be disclosed only for roles paying under NT$40,000/month (Employment Services Act Art. 5), plus a general equal-pay duty; no pay-gap reporting.
ratingNotes.workingTime: 8/40 hours, 46-54 hour monthly overtime caps, statutory premiums, a 7-day rest rule and minute-level attendance records; no exempt category for engineers apart from narrow MOL-approved Art. 84-1 roles.
ratingNotes.leave: Seniority-based annual leave with mandatory payout of unused days, 16 paid holidays, many paid and unpaid statutory leaves, and new 2026 flexibility rules (day-based parental leave, hourly family care, sick-leave protection).
ratingNotes.immigration: The Employment Gold Card and the Foreign Professionals Act make hiring skilled foreigners relatively easy; the 2025 amendments (in force 2026) liberalized them further. PRC nationals are effectively barred.
ratingNotes.changeVelocity: 2025-26 saw new holidays, leave reforms, a workplace-bullying law, the PDPA overhaul, foreign-talent amendments, annual minimum-wage increases and a growing national-security technology list.

keyFacts.label: Employment model
keyFacts.value: No at-will. Indefinite-term employment is the default under the LSA, which covers virtually all private-sector employees, including engineers and most managers. Only true mandated managers (委任經理人 appointed under the Company Act) fall outside the LSA, and courts look at actual subordination, not titles.

keyFacts.label: Contracts & offer letters
keyFacts.value: No statutory writing requirement for the contract itself, but Enforcement Rules Art. 7 lists the terms to agree (duties, place, hours, wages, leave, termination and so on), and non-competes and minimum-service clauses must be in writing. Fixed-term contracts are allowed only for temporary (≤6 months), short-term (≤6 months), seasonal (≤9 months) or specific work (over 1 year needs authority filing). Renewals with gaps of 30 days or less and combined service over 90 days convert the contract to indefinite-term (LSA Art. 9).

keyFacts.label: Probation
keyFacts.value: Not statutory. Under MOL interpretation, parties may agree a reasonable probation period (market practice is 3 months), but ending employment during or at the end of it still needs an LSA Art. 11 or 12 ground (usually Art. 11(5) incompetence), plus Art. 16 notice once tenure reaches 3 months and pro-rated severance.

keyFacts.label: Notice (employer)
keyFacts.value: LSA Art. 16: 10 days for 3 months to under 1 year of service, 20 days for 1-3 years, and 30 days for 3+ years; wages in lieu are allowed. During notice the employee may take up to 2 days of paid job-seeking leave per week. No notice or severance for Art. 12 misconduct dismissals.

keyFacts.label: Notice (employee)
keyFacts.value: The same Art. 16 scale (10/20/30 days) applies to employee resignations from indefinite contracts (Art. 15). Contractual periods longer than the statute are generally unenforceable as a restraint. Employees under a fixed-term contract longer than 3 years may leave after 3 years on 30 days' notice.

keyFacts.label: Statutory severance
keyFacts.value: Payable only for Art. 11 (economic or incompetence) and Art. 14 (constructive) terminations. Labor Pension Act new system (service since 1 July 2005): 0.5 month's average wage per year of service, pro-rated, capped at 6 months (LPA Art. 12). Old system (LSA Art. 17, pre-2005 seniority retained): 1 month per year. Must be paid within 30 days of termination.

keyFacts.label: Working hours & overtime
keyFacts.value: Standard hours are 8/day and 40/week, with a 30-minute break after 4 hours and 11 hours between shifts. Overtime needs union or labor-management-meeting consent and is capped at 12 hours/day total and 46 hours/month, or 54/month and 138 per 3 months with that consent (30+ employee sites must file with the local authority). Premiums: weekday hours 1-2 ≥1⅓x, hours 3-4 ≥1⅔x; rest day hours 1-2 +1⅓, hours 3-8 +1⅔, hours 9-12 +2⅔; holiday work is double pay.

keyFacts.label: Minimum wage
keyFacts.value: From 1 January 2026: NT$29,500/month and NT$196/hour, up from NT$28,590 and NT$190 in 2025 (Minimum Wage Act; 10th straight increase). The rate is set yearly by the Minimum Wage Deliberation Committee in Q3 and takes effect on 1 January.

keyFacts.label: Annual leave
keyFacts.value: LSA Art. 38: 3 days after 6 months of service, 7 after 1 year, 10 after 2, 14 after 3-4, 15 after 5-9, then +1 day a year from 10 years up to 30. The employee chooses the timing. Unused days must be paid out at the end of the leave year or on termination; they may be deferred one year by agreement, then paid. Leave taken and payouts must be recorded and notified to employees in writing each year.

keyFacts.label: Public holidays
keyFacts.value: 16 paid national holidays since the Act on the Implementation of Commemorative and Festival Holidays took effect on 28 May 2025. It added the day before Lunar New Year's Eve, Teachers' Day (Sept 28), Retrocession Day (Oct 25) and Constitution Day (Dec 25), and extended Labor Day to all sectors. Holidays falling on a regular day off or rest day require a make-up day; work on a holiday is paid double.

keyFacts.label: Sick leave
keyFacts.value: Ordinary sick leave: up to 30 days/year non-hospitalized at half pay; hospitalized leave up to 1 year within 2 years (Regulations of Leave-Taking by Workers). From 1 January 2026, taking up to 10 sick days a year cannot lead to adverse treatment in appraisal, promotion or transfer, and attendance bonuses may only be reduced pro rata. Work-injury leave is on full pay (LSA Art. 59).

keyFacts.label: Parental leave
keyFacts.value: Maternity leave: 8 weeks, full pay after 6 months of service (half pay before). Prenatal check-up leave and paternity (accompanying) leave: 7 days paid each. Unpaid parental leave: up to 2 years per child before age 3, with an Employment Insurance allowance of 60% plus a 20% government top-up (80% of average insured salary) for up to 6 months per parent. From 2026, up to 30 days can be taken in single-day units with 5 days' notice.

keyFacts.label: Social insurance / mandatory benefits
keyFacts.value: Labor Insurance: 11.5% ordinary rate plus 1% Employment Insurance, on insured salary capped at NT$45,800, split 70% employer / 20% employee / 10% government. Occupational Accident Insurance is 100% employer-paid (industry rate + 0.07%, cap NT$72,800). NHI is 5.17% (employer 60%, with a dependants factor); supplementary premium is 2.11%. Labor Pension: employer contributes at least 6% of wage (cap NT$150,000), and employees may add up to 6% voluntarily with tax deferral.

keyFacts.label: Payroll frequency & final pay
keyFacts.value: Wages must be paid in full, in cash/NTD, directly to the employee, at least twice a month unless monthly payment is agreed (the norm), with an itemized pay statement (LSA Art. 22-23). On termination, wages must be settled immediately (Enforcement Rules Art. 9), including unused annual leave; severance is due within 30 days.

keyFacts.label: Employee representation
keyFacts.value: Labor-management meetings are mandatory for all employers: equal labor/management representatives, meetings at least quarterly, and they must approve overtime, flexible-hours schemes and other LSA flexibilities. Enterprise unions may form (30+ members); collective agreements are rare in foreign tech offices. An Employee Welfare Committee is expected under the Employee Welfare Fund Act.

keyFacts.label: Data privacy law
keyFacts.value: Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA). Sensitive data (health, medical, genetic, sex life, criminal records) needs a statutory basis or written consent; notice is required at collection. The 2023 amendment raised fines up to NT$15M. The 2025 amendment (promulgated 11 Nov 2025) creates the independent Personal Data Protection Commission and mandatory breach reporting; its effective date is set by the Executive Yuan (verify current status).

keyFacts.label: Record retention
keyFacts.value: Employee roster (LSA Art. 7): 5 years after departure. Wage records (Art. 23): 5 years. Attendance records to the minute (Art. 30): 5 years, and employees may request copies. Health exam records: at least 7 years (longer for special hazards). Under the Labor Incident Act, missing records shift the risk of proof to the employer.

keyFacts.label: Non-competes & IP
keyFacts.value: Post-employment non-competes are valid only if they meet LSA Art. 9-1: legitimate interest, a role with access to trade secrets, reasonable scope and a maximum of 2 years, compensation of at least 50% of average monthly wage (not paid during employment), and a written agreement. Otherwise they are void. The employer owns service inventions but owes 'appropriate remuneration' unless the contract says otherwise (Patent Act Art. 7). Employees are the authors of work-made copyrights unless the contract names the employer as author (Copyright Act Art. 11).

keyFacts.label: Language requirements
keyFacts.value: No statutory language rule for employment contracts, but work rules filed with the authority, notices and labor-management meeting materials must be in Traditional Chinese in practice. Bilingual contracts and policies are recommended, and the Chinese version is what courts and inspectors rely on.

keyFacts.label: Regulator(s)
keyFacts.value: Ministry of Labor (MOL): Workforce Development Agency (foreign work permits), Occupational Safety and Health Administration, Bureau of Labor Insurance. Local labor departments (Taipei City, New Taipei, Hsinchu), and the Science Park Bureau for companies inside Hsinchu Science Park. Also the National Health Insurance Administration, Ministry of Finance/National Taxation Bureau, National Development Council and National Immigration Agency (foreign talent), PDPC Preparatory Office, NSTC/MOEA (core key technologies), MJIB and the Mainland Affairs Council (cross-strait enforcement).

mandatoryPolicies.name: Work rules (工作規則)
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Employers with 30+ employees must adopt work rules covering hours, leave, wages, overtime, discipline, attendance, termination, severance, retirement, welfare and safety. They must be filed with the local labor authority for approval within 30 days of reaching 30 employees and posted publicly. Global policies are not enforceable locally unless incorporated.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Labor Standards Act Art. 70; Enforcement Rules Art. 37

mandatoryPolicies.name: Labor-management meetings
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: All employers must hold labor-management meetings at least once every 3 months, with elected employee representatives in equal numbers to management and the membership reported to the local authority. Consent from this meeting (where there is no union) is needed for overtime, flexible working-hours schemes and shift-rest adjustments.
mandatoryPolicies.source: LSA Art. 83; Regulations for Implementing Labor-Management Meetings

mandatoryPolicies.name: Sexual harassment prevention
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: 10+ employees: set up and publicize a complaint channel. 30+ employees: also adopt and post prevention measures, complaint procedures and disciplinary rules. On a complaint, protect the complainant, investigate, discipline, and notify the local authority of the complaint and outcome. Complaints against the highest-ranking responsible person can go directly to the local authority.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 13, 32-1 (2023 amendments, effective 8 Mar 2024)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Workplace bullying prevention
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: From 1 July 2026: 10+ employees must set up and publicize a bullying complaint channel. 30+ employees must adopt and disclose prevention measures, complaint and investigation procedures and disciplinary rules. Complaints must be investigated and registered in MOL's reporting system, and cases against the top responsible person go to the local authority.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Occupational Safety and Health Act, workplace bullying chapter (amended Dec 2025); Workplace Bullying Prevention Measures Standards

mandatoryPolicies.name: Unlawful infringement (workplace violence) prevention
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Employers must plan and take measures to prevent physical or verbal violence during work. Sites with 100+ workers need a written prevention plan and implementation records; smaller sites may use execution records.
mandatoryPolicies.source: OSH Act Art. 6(2); OSH Act Enforcement Rules

mandatoryPolicies.name: Overwork (abnormal workload) prevention
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Identify and assess high-risk employees (long hours, shifts, night work), arrange physician interviews, and adjust work. 100+ workers: written plan.
mandatoryPolicies.source: OSH Act Art. 6(2)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Maternal health protection
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Assess and control hazards for pregnant and post-partum (1 year) workers, including physician assessment and job adjustment. A written program is required at larger sites (100+) and for hazardous work.
mandatoryPolicies.source: OSH Act Art. 30-31; Rules for Maternal Health Protection at Workplaces

mandatoryPolicies.name: Occupational health services & OSH management
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Workplaces with 50-299 workers must contract physician/nurse on-site health services at prescribed frequencies; 300+ must employ nurses and employ or contract physicians. Designate OSH management personnel according to risk category and headcount; offices are low-risk, labs and fab areas higher.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Labor Health Protection Rules; Regulations of Occupational Safety and Health Management

mandatoryPolicies.name: Working time, overtime & attendance recording
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Record attendance to the minute (including remote work), obtain the consent needed for overtime and flexible schedules, track the 46/54/138-hour caps, and pay premiums or offer comp time at the employee's choice.

mandatoryPolicies.name: Leave policy (statutory leaves)
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: The policy must cover annual leave with payout, 16 holidays with make-up days, sick leave with the 2026 anti-retaliation rules and pro-rated attendance bonus, menstrual, marriage, bereavement, maternity, prenatal, paternity, family care (hourly from 2026) and parental leave (day-based from 2026).
mandatoryPolicies.source: LSA Art. 37-43, 50; Regulations of Leave-Taking by Workers; Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 14-20

mandatoryPolicies.name: Personal data protection & security maintenance
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Employee privacy notice, legal basis or written consent for sensitive data, security maintenance measures, and a breach response plan with notice to data subjects. Prepare for PDPC reporting (draft rules propose 72 hours).
mandatoryPolicies.source: Personal Data Protection Act Art. 6, 8, 12, 27 (as amended 2023 and 2025)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Non-compete & minimum-service agreements
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: If used, they must meet Art. 9-1 conditions (written, 2-year maximum, at least 50% compensation) and Art. 15-1 conditions (minimum service only in return for employer-funded specialized training or reasonable compensation, for a reasonable period).
mandatoryPolicies.source: LSA Art. 9-1, 15-1; Enforcement Rules Art. 7-1 to 7-3

mandatoryPolicies.name: Trade secret protection program
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Information qualifies as a trade secret only if 'reasonable protective measures' exist, and a company can avoid corporate fines only by showing it did its best to prevent misappropriation. Classification, access control, NDAs, monitoring notice, training and exit procedures are all expected.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Trade Secrets Act Art. 2, 13-1, 13-2, 13-4

mandatoryPolicies.name: National core key technology controls
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Identify whether any work touches listed national core key technologies (e.g., AI/HPC chip design, chiplet interconnect, advanced packaging). Apply enhanced access controls, and track Cross-Strait Act travel-approval duties for staff on government-commissioned or subsidized core key technology projects.
mandatoryPolicies.source: National Security Act Art. 3, 8; Act Governing Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area Art. 9, 91

mandatoryPolicies.name: Anti-discrimination & recruitment rules
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: No discrimination on the Art. 5 grounds, no withholding of ID documents or requests for non-job-related private information, and salary-range disclosure for postings paying under NT$40,000/month.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Employment Services Act Art. 5

mandatoryPolicies.name: Lactation and childcare measures
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Grant 60 minutes a day of paid lactation time (child under 2). Employers with 100+ employees must provide lactation rooms and childcare facilities or measures (e.g., childcare subsidies or contracted daycare).
mandatoryPolicies.source: Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 18, 23

mandatoryPolicies.name: Disability employment quota
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Private employers with 67+ employees must employ persons with disabilities equal to at least 1% of headcount (minimum 1), or pay the shortfall (monthly minimum wage per missing person) into the disability employment fund.
mandatoryPolicies.source: People with Disabilities Rights Protection Act Art. 38, 43

mandatoryPolicies.name: Employee Welfare Committee / welfare fund
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Enterprises are expected to set aside employee welfare funds from capital, revenue and a 0.5% employee wage deduction, administered by an employee welfare committee. Enforcement against foreign-owned service entities varies; take local advice.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Employee Welfare Fund Act (職工福利金條例)

mandatoryPolicies.name: Social insurance & pension enrollment
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Enroll Labor Insurance, Occupational Accident Insurance, Employment Insurance and NHI from the first day of work. Report labor pension contributions within 7 days of hire or separation.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Labor Insurance Act; Labor Occupational Accident Insurance and Protection Act; NHI Act; Labor Pension Act Art. 18

mandatoryPolicies.name: Layoff notification & mass redundancy plan
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Report every individual layoff to the local authority and public employment service 10 days before the separation date. Where Mass Redundancy Protection Act thresholds are met, give the plan to authorities, the union or representatives and employees 60 days ahead, and negotiate.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Employment Services Act Art. 33; Mass Redundancy Protection Act Art. 2, 4, 5

mandatoryPolicies.name: Equal pay & anti-retaliation for family leave
mandatoryPolicies.requirement: Equal pay for work of equal value regardless of gender. No adverse treatment for requesting or taking maternity, parental, family care or menstrual leave, or for filing harassment complaints.
mandatoryPolicies.source: Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 10, 21, 36

hiring.detail: Screen out interview questions and application-form fields on marital status, pregnancy plans, horoscope, blood type, age and similar. Never hold passports or ID cards. Fines for discrimination run NT$300,000-1,500,000.
Postings for roles with regular pay under NT$40,000/month must show a salary range. Customer-support postings may be affected.
Do not use fixed-term contracts for ongoing engineering or support roles, because courts convert them. Fixed-term is only for temporary, short-term, seasonal or specific-project work.

hiring.req: Written offer and contract with core terms
hiring.detail: Cover duties, work location (with a reasonable transfer clause), hours and overtime approval, wage components (note which are 'wages' for severance), bonus eligibility, leave and termination. Provide a Traditional Chinese version.

hiring.req: Background checks with notice and consent
hiring.detail: Give a PDPA notice. Criminal record and health data are sensitive and need written consent or a statutory basis. Keep checks job-related and proportionate.

Have hires from TSMC, MediaTek, UMC and similar firms certify that they bring no prior-employer materials. Wall off sensitive projects where needed, and check any existing Art. 9-1 non-compete and paid restraint.
hiring.cite: Trade Secrets Act Art. 13-1, 13-2; National Security Act Art. 3

hiring.detail: Obtain a WDA work permit for specialized work (salary threshold currently NT$47,971/month; verify) or use an Employment Gold Card. Arrange the residence permit (ARC). 2026 amendments widen eligibility for graduates of top global universities.
hiring.cite: Employment Services Act Art. 46; Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals

hiring.detail: Employer-paid health exam at hiring, with results handled as sensitive data.
hiring.cite: OSH Act Art. 20; Labor Health Protection Rules

onboarding.detail: Enroll Labor Insurance, Employment Insurance and Occupational Accident Insurance with BLI, and NHI, effective the first day of work, at the correct insured-salary grade. Late enrollment makes the employer liable for lost benefits.
onboarding.cite: Labor Insurance Act; Labor Occupational Accident Insurance and Protection Act; NHI Act

onboarding.detail: Report within 7 days and contribute at least 6% of monthly wage (per the grade table, cap NT$150,000) to the employee's individual account. Offer the voluntary employee contribution of up to 6%.
Create the statutory employee roster (勞工名卡) with personal details, wage and leave history. Keep it 5 years after departure.
Provide the approved work rules, harassment and bullying complaint channels, leave and overtime approval procedures, and get acknowledgments.
onboarding.cite: LSA Art. 70; Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 13

onboarding.detail: Name the employer as author of work-made copyrights, cover service inventions and remuneration, include a trade-secret acknowledgment, and describe monitoring/DLP with a PDPA notice.
onboarding.cite: Copyright Act Art. 11; Patent Act Art. 7-8; Trade Secrets Act

onboarding.detail: Deliver general OSH training for new hires (typically at least 3 hours for general workers), with extra training for lab or hazardous work.
onboarding.cite: OSH Act Art. 32; Regulations for OSH Education and Training

onboarding.detail: Determine resident vs non-resident status (183-day rule). Non-residents are withheld at a flat 18% (6% if pay is at or below 1.5x the minimum wage); residents under the withholding tables.
onboarding.cite: Income Tax Act; Withholding Rates Standards

payAndPayroll.req: Pay at least the minimum wage
payAndPayroll.detail: NT$29,500/month and NT$196/hour from 1 January 2026. Check part-timers, interns and anyone insured at the lowest grade.
Pay in NTD, in full and directly, on a fixed payday (monthly by agreement), with an itemized statement. No pre-deduction of damages or penalties from wages.
Weekday: hours 1-2 at ≥1⅓x, hours 3-4 at ≥1⅔x. Rest day: hours 1-2 +1⅓, hours 3-8 +1⅔, hours 9-12 +2⅔. Comp time only if the employee chooses it; unused comp time must be paid.
Work on one of the 16 holidays or on an annual-leave day scheduled with consent: an extra full day's wage. Regular day off (例假): emergencies only, with double pay and compensatory rest.
Deduct the employee shares of Labor Insurance/EI (20%) and NHI (30%, including dependants). Pay the employer shares plus the 0.025% wage arrears fund levy monthly.
payAndPayroll.cite: Labor Insurance Act; NHI Act; LSA Art. 28

payAndPayroll.detail: Withhold 2.11% on bonuses exceeding 4x the monthly insured amount in a year. The employer also pays 2.11% on total payroll minus total insured salaries.

LSA Art. 29 requires a bonus or profit share for fault-free employees when the business earns a net profit. A Taiwan company must state an employee-compensation percentage of profit in its articles, decided by the board.
Audit pay for gender gaps in equal-value roles; complaints go to the local gender equality committee.
payAndPayroll.cite: Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 10

timeAndLeave.detail: 8 hours/day and 40/week; a 30-minute break after 4 hours; 11 hours between shifts. Flexible 2-week, 8-week or 4-week schemes need union or labor-management-meeting consent.

Maximum 12 hours/day including overtime. Up to 46 hours/month, or 54/month and 138 per quarter with consent (file with the authority at 30+ employees). Employees may refuse overtime for health or other legitimate reasons.
One regular day off (例假) plus one rest day (休息日) in every 7 days; the regular day off can be worked only in emergencies. Evening calls with US HQ count as working time.

timeAndLeave.req: Annual leave by seniority, with payout
timeAndLeave.detail: 3/7/10/14/15 days rising to 30. The employee decides timing, unused leave is paid out, and the annual written leave statement is mandatory.
Update the 2026 calendar: the day before Lunar New Year's Eve, Teachers' Day, Retrocession Day and Constitution Day are paid holidays, with make-up days when they fall on a day off.
timeAndLeave.cite: Act on the Implementation of Commemorative and Festival Holidays (2025); LSA Art. 37; Enforcement Rules Art. 23-1

timeAndLeave.detail: 30 days/year at half pay (non-hospitalized). Up to 10 days/year cannot trigger adverse appraisal, promotion or transfer decisions, and attendance bonuses are reduced only pro rata.
timeAndLeave.cite: LSA Art. 43; Regulations of Leave-Taking by Workers Art. 4, 9-1 (2026)

timeAndLeave.req: Menstrual, marriage, bereavement and personal leave
timeAndLeave.detail: Menstrual leave: 1 day/month at half pay, 3 days/year outside the sick-leave count. Marriage: 8 days paid. Bereavement: 3-8 days paid by relationship. Personal leave: 14 days unpaid.
timeAndLeave.cite: Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 14; Regulations of Leave-Taking by Workers

timeAndLeave.detail: Maternity: 8 weeks (full pay after 6 months of service). Miscarriage leave: 4 weeks to 5 days depending on gestation. Prenatal check-up leave: 7 days paid. Paternity/accompanying leave: 7 days paid.
timeAndLeave.cite: LSA Art. 50; Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 15

timeAndLeave.req: Parental and family care leave (2026 flexibility)
timeAndLeave.detail: Unpaid parental leave up to 2 years per child under 3, of which up to 30 days per parent can be taken in single days with 5 days' notice (shorter in emergencies). Family care leave: 7 days/year, usable hourly up to 56 hours. Employers cannot refuse or penalize.
timeAndLeave.cite: Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 16, 20; Regulations for Implementing Parental Leave Without Pay

timeAndLeave.detail: Record start, end and overtime to the minute, including remote work (electronic logs are acceptable). Retain 5 years. Under the Labor Incident Act, recorded time is presumed working time.
timeAndLeave.cite: LSA Art. 30; Labor Incident Act Art. 38

benefits.req: Labor, employment and occupational accident insurance
benefits.detail: Labor Insurance at 11.5% plus EI at 1% (70/20/10 split), insured salary NT$29,500-45,800. Occupational accident insurance is employer-paid, with a cap of NT$72,800.
benefits.cite: Labor Insurance Act; Employment Insurance Act; Labor Occupational Accident Insurance and Protection Act

benefits.detail: 5.17% premium on an insured amount of up to NT$313,000 (2026 table; verify). Employer pays 60% including an average dependants factor. Covers foreign employees with an ARC from their start date.

At least 6% employer contribution to a portable individual account (Taiwan nationals, foreign spouses and APRC holders). 2025 amendments extend coverage to more foreign professionals; confirm eligibility per hire.
benefits.cite: Labor Pension Act Art. 6-7, 14; Act for the Recruitment and Employment of Foreign Professionals (2025 amend.)

benefits.detail: General checks every 5 years under age 40, every 3 years at 40-64 and yearly at 65+, at employer cost. Special checks for hazardous work.
benefits.cite: OSH Act Art. 20; Labor Health Protection Rules

benefits.detail: Establish an employee welfare committee to fund festivals, travel and allowances. Market practice includes Dragon Boat and Mid-Autumn festival gifts or bonuses.
At 100+ employees, provide a lactation room and childcare facilities or measures (typically a childcare subsidy or partner daycare).
benefits.cite: Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 18, 23

benefits.detail: Group life, accident and medical insurance, an annual health check more generous than the statute, and extra paid sick or family days are standard for chip employers competing with TSMC and MediaTek.
US-parent RSUs are a key differentiator against local profit-sharing cultures. Communicate the Taiwan tax treatment of vesting income and check for NHI and reporting obligations with tax advisors.
benefits.cite: Income Tax Act; Company Act Art. 235-1

performanceAndConduct.req: Discipline must be in the work rules and proportionate
performanceAndConduct.detail: Only discipline for conduct listed in the approved work rules. Serious-misconduct dismissal must fit an LSA Art. 12 ground and satisfy the 30-day rule.
Before an Art. 11(5) incompetence dismissal, courts expect clear objective standards, coaching or training, a genuine improvement plan, and consideration of reassignment (last-resort principle).

A transfer must be for business need and not improper motive, keep wages and terms no worse, suit the employee's physical and technical ability, offer help if the location changes, and consider family life.
From 2026, employers may not downgrade appraisals, promotions or transfers because of up to 10 days' sick leave. Evaluations must weigh overall performance.
performanceAndConduct.cite: Regulations of Leave-Taking by Workers Art. 9-1

performanceAndConduct.detail: Take immediate and effective corrective measures, investigate impartially (MOL expects about 2 months, extendable 1 month; verify), notify the local authority of the complaint and result, and protect against retaliation.
performanceAndConduct.cite: Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 13, 36

performanceAndConduct.detail: Offer mediation where appropriate, take interim protective measures, and investigate with at least half external members on investigation committees where required. Register the case in MOL's reporting system. Fines run NT$30,000-750,000 for employer failures and up to NT$1M for a top executive who bullies.
performanceAndConduct.cite: OSH Act workplace bullying chapter; Workplace Bullying Prevention Measures Standards

performanceAndConduct.detail: Email, endpoint and DLP monitoring should be disclosed in policy and the PDPA notice, and kept proportionate to trade-secret protection. Covert monitoring risks privacy claims.

termination.detail: Grounds: business suspension or transfer; losses or contraction; force majeure suspension of 1+ month; change in business nature with no suitable position; or clear incompetence. The employer must show redeployment was considered.

Grounds: misrepresentation at hiring, violence or insults, final prison sentence, serious breach of contract or work rules, intentional damage or leaking of technical or confidential information, or 3 consecutive (6 per month) unexcused absences. Act within 30 days of learning the facts; no notice or severance.
10/20/30 days by tenure, or pay in lieu. Up to 2 days/week of paid job-seeking leave during notice.

New system: 0.5 month's average wage per year (pro-rated, capped at 6 months). The average wage includes overtime and recurring allowances from the last 6 months. Late or unpaid severance: fines of NT$300,000-1,500,000.
termination.cite: Labor Pension Act Art. 12; LSA Art. 17, 78

termination.detail: No termination during the 8-week maternity leave or occupational-injury treatment period, except for natural disaster or force majeure making the business impossible. No termination for pregnancy, parental leave or complaints.
termination.cite: LSA Art. 13; Gender Equality in Employment Act Art. 11, 21

termination.detail: Report each Art. 11 layoff (name, role, reason, need for job assistance) to the local authority and public employment service at least 10 days before the separation date. Fines NT$30,000-150,000.

Triggered within a 60-day period at a site: more than 10 layoffs (under 30 staff); more than 1/3 or 20 in one day (30-199 staff); more than 1/4 or 50 in one day (200-499); more than 1/5 or 80 in one day (500+); or more than 200 (or 100 in a day) enterprise-wide. Then the 60-day plan notice and negotiation apply.

Often the preferred route. Document the employer's initiative and the reason code so the employee can claim EI unemployment benefits, pay statutory entitlements plus an ex gratia amount, and use Chinese and English versions.
termination.cite: Civil Code Art. 736; Employment Insurance Act Art. 11

exit.detail: Pay all wages, overtime and unused annual leave immediately on termination (in practice by the next payroll at the latest). Severance is due within 30 days.
exit.cite: LSA Enforcement Rules Art. 9, 24-1; LSA Art. 17

exit.detail: On request, issue a certificate of service (dates, position). The employer may not refuse or include adverse remarks the employee did not ask for.
For Art. 11 or 13 terminations and employer-initiated mutual separations, issue a separation certificate stating the involuntary reason so the employee can claim unemployment benefits.
Withdraw Labor, EI and occupational accident insurance and NHI on the last day. Stop pension contributions and report within 7 days.
exit.cite: Labor Insurance Act; Labor Pension Act Art. 18; NHI Act

exit.detail: If enforcing an Art. 9-1 non-compete, pay at least 50% of the average monthly wage for the restricted period, lump sum or monthly; otherwise the clause is void.

Recover devices, revoke access, get a written return and non-retention certification, review recent downloads under the disclosed monitoring policy, and remind the employee of confidentiality and National Security Act exposure.
exit.cite: Trade Secrets Act; National Security Act

exit.detail: Include departed employees in the January withholding statement filing. For departing foreign residents, settle tax before exit (departure tax clearance).

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Employee roster: 5 years after departure. Wage records and attendance records: 5 years each. Employees may request attendance copies, and the employer must produce them in labor litigation.

Give a notice at collection (purpose, categories, use period and area, rights). Rely on contract or legal obligation for core HR data; written consent is required for sensitive data such as health exams.

recordsAndPrivacy.req: Breach response and upcoming PDPC reporting
recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Notify affected individuals now. Once the 2025 amendment is effective, also report to the PDPC; draft rules (Feb 2026) propose 72 hours for sensitive data, 10,000+ records or 100+ affected people.
recordsAndPrivacy.cite: Personal Data Protection Act Art. 12 (2025 amend.); PDPC draft Personal Data Breach Notification Regulations

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Keep a documented security program covering access control, audits, training and an incident plan. Fines reach up to NT$15M for failures that are not corrected, and draft PDPC rules add risk assessments for large holders.
recordsAndPrivacy.cite: Personal Data Protection Act Art. 27, 48 (2023 amend.)

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Generally permitted unless restricted by the regulator. Disclose transfers in the notice and use intra-group agreements; the PDPC takes over cross-border rules once the amendment is effective.
Keep health exam records at least 7 years (longer for special hazards), and keep harassment and bullying files confidential with restricted access.
recordsAndPrivacy.cite: Labor Health Protection Rules; Gender Equality in Employment Act

recordsAndPrivacy.detail: Delete or anonymize candidate and former-employee data once retention periods and litigation windows lapse. Labor claims generally run 5 years for wages.
recordsAndPrivacy.cite: Personal Data Protection Act Art. 11; Civil Code Art. 126

healthSafety.detail: Maintain an OSH plan and designate management personnel for the site's risk category. Offices are low-risk, while labs, test and fab areas (electronic component manufacturing) are high-risk.
healthSafety.cite: OSH Act Art. 5-6, 23; Regulations of Occupational Safety and Health Management

healthSafety.detail: Hazard assessment and a reporting and response process. A written plan is required at 100+ workers, covering customer-facing support staff as well.
Screen long-hours and night or shift staff, arrange physician interviews, and adjust workloads. This is relevant for teams running follow-the-sun support with US HQ.
Risk-assess pregnant and post-partum employees and adjust duties. No night work (10pm-6am) for pregnant or breastfeeding employees.
50-299 workers: contracted physician/nurse visits. 300+: employ nurses and employ or contract physicians.
Complaint channel at 10+, full prevention and discipline rules at 30+, case registration with MOL, and external investigators. The rules also cover remote work and client sites.
Report to the labor inspection agency within 8 hours for a death, 3+ injured, or 1+ hospitalized.
No-fault employer liability for medical costs and wage replacement, offset by occupational accident insurance benefits.
healthSafety.cite: LSA Art. 59; Labor Occupational Accident Insurance and Protection Act

terminationDeepDive.voluntary: Employees on indefinite contracts resign by giving the Art. 16 notice (10/20/30 days by tenure). Employer acceptance is not required, and longer contractual notice or resignation penalties are generally unenforceable. The employer may waive the notice and release the employee early by agreement while paying through the agreed date. Garden leave is possible with full pay, but the employee remains employed and accrues leave. Employees may resign without notice and claim severance for employer breaches such as unpaid wages or insurance, abuse or unsafe work (Art. 14).
terminationDeepDive.involuntary: Termination is only lawful on an Art. 11 ground (with notice and severance) or an Art. 12 ground (without notice or severance, within 30 days of learning the facts for most grounds). Courts apply the last-resort principle: document objective standards, coaching, warnings and redeployment options. An invalid dismissal leaves the contract in force, with back pay (Civil Code Art. 487). Under the Labor Incident Act, employees can sue in specialized labor courts after mandatory mediation (usually completed within 3 months) and obtain provisional orders to continue employment during the case. Probation terminations follow the same rules.
terminationDeepDive.redundancy: Individual redundancy uses Art. 11(2) or (4): show genuine business need, consider redeployment, give notice, pay severance, and file the Employment Services Act Art. 33 notification 10 days before separation. Collective layoff under the Mass Redundancy Protection Act is triggered by 60-day thresholds (for example, more than 1/5 of staff or 80 in one day at 500+ sites; more than 1/3 or 20 in one day at 30-199 sites; more than 10 at sites under 30). Then give the layoff plan to the labor authority, the union (or labor-management-meeting labor representatives, or all employees) and post it 60 days in advance. Negotiate within 10 days, after which the authority may convene a negotiation committee. Selection must not discriminate, and responsible persons of employers who fail to pay wages or severance above statutory thresholds can face exit bans.
terminationDeepDive.finalPayTiming: Wages (including overtime and unused annual leave) must be settled immediately on termination (Enforcement Rules Art. 9); in practice by the last day or next payroll. Severance is due within 30 days (LSA Art. 17; LPA Art. 12). Penalties: unpaid wages NT$20,000-1,000,000 (LSA Art. 79); unpaid severance NT$300,000-1,500,000 with repeat fines (LSA Art. 78; LPA Art. 45-1), plus public naming of the employer (LSA Art. 80-1).
requiredDocuments: Written termination notice citing the specific LSA Art. 11 or 12 ground and effective date (Chinese version recommended)
Employment Services Act Art. 33 layoff notification to the local authority and public employment service (Art. 11 layoffs, 10 days before separation)
Certificate of service (LSA Art. 19), on request
Involuntary separation certificate for Employment Insurance unemployment benefits (where applicable)
Final pay statement itemizing wages, overtime, unused annual leave and severance
Labor/EI/occupational accident insurance and NHI withdrawal and labor pension stop-contribution filings
Mass redundancy plan and filing (where thresholds are met)
Non-compete compensation notice and payment schedule (if enforcing an Art. 9-1 restraint)
terminationDeepDive.releaseAgreements: Settlement agreements (Civil Code Art. 736) are enforceable if voluntary and informed. Rights under mandatory law cannot be waived in advance, but accrued claims can be settled. There is no statutory review or revocation period, though agreements induced by fraud or duress can be rescinded (Civil Code Art. 92). Best practice: bilingual text, an itemized list of statutory amounts plus any ex gratia payment, a clear reason code, confidentiality and non-disparagement, and return-of-property clauses. A settlement recorded in labor mediation or court has the force of a final judgment.
terminationDeepDive.typicalPackage: Market practice (not statutory, verify with local benchmarking): for tech and semiconductor employers, restructuring exits usually pay statutory notice pay plus new-system severance plus pro-rated bonus plus unused leave, topped up with an ex gratia amount of about 1-3 months' salary (sometimes 1 month per year of service for senior staff). Packages are often framed as mutual separations to reduce reinstatement risk. Unvested US RSUs usually lapse under plan terms, though some companies accelerate a tranche.

recentChanges.title: Investigators probe 17 China-funded firms for talent poaching
recentChanges.detail: MJIB searched 64 locations and questioned 114 people in July-August 2026 over PRC-linked firms covertly recruiting Taiwan chip and tech talent, after a March 2025 probe of 11 firms including SMIC. Cross-Strait Act and National Security Act enforcement is intensifying.

recentChanges.title: Workplace bullying chapter of OSH Act in force
recentChanges.detail: In force from 1 July 2026 with two implementing regulations. It defines workplace bullying, requires a complaint channel at 10+ employees and prevention, complaint, investigation and discipline rules at 30+, case registration in MOL's system, local-authority handling when the top executive is accused, and higher fines.

recentChanges.title: First corporate conviction under National Security Act core-technology provisions
recentChanges.detail: The IP and Commercial Court sentenced a former TSMC engineer to 10 years (others to 2-6 years) for leaking 2nm process secrets to Tokyo Electron. TEL Taiwan faced a NT$150M penalty, the first case against a corporate entity for core key technology misappropriation.

recentChanges.title: PDPC pre-announces security and breach-notification rules
recentChanges.detail: Draft rules propose 72-hour breach reporting for sensitive data, systems with 10,000+ records or incidents affecting 100+ people, plus baseline security measures and extra requirements for large data holders. The 60-day comment period ran from 6 February 2026.

recentChanges.title: National core key technologies list amended again
recentChanges.detail: NSTC pre-announced expanding the list from 32 to 42 items (November 2025, covering defense, space, agriculture, semiconductors, cybersecurity, quantum, energy and AI). The NSTC regulations database shows an amended list published in early 2026; confirm the final items.

recentChanges.title: Minimum wage NT$29,500/month, NT$196/hour
recentChanges.detail: Up 3.18% from NT$28,590/NT$190, the 10th consecutive increase. Labor Insurance, occupational accident insurance and NHI lowest grades also rose to NT$29,500.

recentChanges.title: Day-based parental leave, hourly family care leave, sick-leave protection
recentChanges.detail: Up to 30 days of unpaid parental leave per parent can be taken in single days, still with the 80% allowance. Family care leave is usable hourly (56 hours/year). Up to 10 sick days/year cannot lead to adverse treatment, and attendance bonuses may only be pro-rated.

recentChanges.title: Foreign Professionals Act amendments take effect
recentChanges.detail: Passed 29 August 2025 and promulgated 24 September 2025; most provisions took effect 1 January 2026 and some on 30 June 2026. Changes: open permits for top-200 university graduates, the experience exemption extended to top-1,500 universities, work rights for spouses, faster APRC (1 year for high earners), and wider Employment Insurance and labor pension coverage.

recentChanges.title: Legislature passes workplace bullying amendments to OSH Act
recentChanges.detail: Workplace bullying defined by statute (early December 2025), with employer fines of NT$30,000-750,000 for failing to act and NT$10,000-1M for top executives who bully.

recentChanges.title: PDPA amendments promulgated
recentChanges.detail: Promulgated 11 November 2025. Creates the independent Personal Data Protection Commission as the regulator, mandates breach reporting to the PDPC, and moves security-maintenance and cross-border rules to it, with a 6-year sector transition. The effective date is to be set by the Executive Yuan.

recentChanges.title: Four new paid national holidays
recentChanges.detail: The Act on the Implementation of Commemorative and Festival Holidays took effect 28 May 2025. It added the day before Lunar New Year's Eve, Teachers' Day (Sept 28), Retrocession Day (Oct 25) and Constitution Day (Dec 25), raising private-sector paid holidays from 12 to 16.

recentChanges.title: Core key technologies list expanded to 32 items
recentChanges.detail: Second-wave list covering, for semiconductors: ≤14nm IC process, heterogeneous integration packaging, AI/HPC chip design, high-bandwidth chiplet interconnect design, GaN/SiC devices, chip security, cryogenic chips and qubits.

recentChanges.title: Gender Equality in Employment Act harassment amendments effective
recentChanges.detail: In force from 8 March 2024: complaint channel at 10+ employees, full prevention and discipline rules at 30+, notification of complaints and outcomes to the local authority, direct complaints to the authority against the highest-ranking manager, and higher fines.

watchlist.title: PDPA amendment effective date and formal PDPC establishment
watchlist.detail: The Executive Yuan must set the effective date and the PDPC organic law must take effect. Final breach-notification (72-hour) and security-maintenance regulations will follow; update incident-response and vendor contracts.

watchlist.title: 2027 minimum wage
watchlist.detail: The Minimum Wage Deliberation Committee meets in Q3 each year. Confirm the 2027 rate announced for 1 January 2027 and the matching insurance grade tables.

watchlist.title: Tax incentive rules for foreign special professionals
watchlist.detail: Draft amendments would widen eligible fields, allow retroactive benefit after a gold card or special permit is approved, and impose a strict claim deadline at annual filing. The 50% exemption on salary above NT$3M for 5 years is unchanged.

watchlist.title: Further core key technology list updates and cross-strait enforcement
watchlist.detail: NSTC reviews the list periodically; watch additions touching chip design, packaging and AI. Also watch proposed Cross-Strait Act tightening on PRC talent poaching and ongoing MJIB raids.

watchlist.title: Workplace bullying enforcement practice
watchlist.detail: First inspections, case-registration data and court rulings under the new OSH chapter will shape investigation standards and external-investigator expectations.

watchlist.title: Labor insurance financing reform
watchlist.detail: Ongoing debate over Labor Insurance fund solvency may bring rate increases (the statute allows up to 13%) or benefit changes.

calendar.title: New minimum wage and insurance grades
calendar.detail: Apply the new minimum wage (NT$29,500/NT$196 for 2026) and updated Labor Insurance, NHI and pension grade tables from 1 January. Re-grade affected employees.

calendar.title: Withholding statements and NHI supplementary premium filing
calendar.detail: File the prior year's income tax withholding and supplementary premium statements with the tax authority by 31 January (next business day if it falls on a holiday). Issue statements to employees by 10 February.

calendar.title: Annual leave settlement (calendar-year schemes)
calendar.detail: Pay out unused prior-year annual leave (unless deferral was agreed) by the regular payday or within 30 days of year-end, and give the written annual leave statement.

calendar.title: Year-end (Lunar New Year) bonuses
calendar.detail: Pay year-end bonuses before the Lunar New Year holiday (late January to February). Check the LSA Art. 29 profit-bonus duty and apply 2.11% NHI supplementary premium withholding on large bonuses.

calendar.title: Q1 labor-management meeting; old-system pension top-up
calendar.detail: Hold the quarterly labor-management meeting. If any employees keep old-system seniority, top up the pension reserve shortfall by 31 March.

calendar.title: Individual income tax filing
calendar.detail: Annual individual income tax filing runs 1-31 May. Foreign professionals claim the special tax incentive with their filing. Labor Day (May 1) is a paid holiday.

calendar.title: Q2 labor-management meeting; Dragon Boat Festival
calendar.detail: Hold the quarterly meeting (approve or renew overtime and flexible-hours consents as needed). Dragon Boat Festival holiday and customary festival bonus or gift (the date moves with the lunar calendar).

calendar.title: Anniversary of bullying rules; mid-year compliance check
calendar.detail: Review workplace bullying (effective 1 July 2026) and sexual harassment case logs, training completion and complaint-channel postings.

calendar.title: Minimum wage decision; Q3 meeting; Mid-Autumn and Teachers' Day
calendar.detail: Budget for the minimum wage decided in Q3. Hold the Q3 labor-management meeting. Mid-Autumn Festival (lunar date) and Teachers' Day (Sept 28) are paid holidays.

calendar.title: National Day and Retrocession Day
calendar.detail: Paid holidays on Oct 10 and Oct 25, with make-up days if they fall on a regular day off or rest day.

calendar.title: Next-year insurance and pension grade tables
calendar.detail: MOL and NHIA publish next year's insured salary and contribution grade tables. Update payroll configuration.

calendar.title: Year-end leave, bonus and Q4 meeting
calendar.detail: Constitution Day (Dec 25) holiday. Hold the Q4 labor-management meeting, confirm annual leave balances and deferrals, finalize year-end bonus and employee-compensation resolutions, and publish next year's holiday calendar (16 days).

calendar.title: Annual health check and OSH plan review
calendar.detail: Schedule periodic health exams and review the workplace violence, overwork, musculoskeletal and maternal health plans and records for the coming year.

gotchas: Treating engineers and support staff as 'exempt'. Taiwan has no salary-based exemption; Art. 84-1 applies only to MOL-designated roles with an authority-approved agreement. Unrecorded evening calls with US HQ, Slack after hours and on-call time create overtime liability, which the Labor Incident Act presumes from attendance records.

Running US-style exits (at-will, 30-day PIP then termination, 'position eliminated' without a real business reason). Dismissals need an Art. 11 or 12 ground and last-resort evidence, and invalid dismissals lead to reinstatement plus back pay.
Missing the Employment Services Act Art. 33 layoff notification 10 days before separation, or not issuing the involuntary-separation certificate employees need for unemployment benefits.
Using global non-compete templates without paying at least 50% of average monthly wage for up to 2 years. Such clauses are void, and a restraint paid during employment does not count.

Assuming global handbooks apply. At 30+ employees, work rules must be filed with the local labor authority (the Science Park Bureau for Hsinchu Science Park sites) and posted. Overtime and flexible schedules need labor-management-meeting consent, and those meetings must actually be held every quarter.
Use-it-or-lose-it annual leave or unpaid forfeiture. Unused statutory leave must be paid out at year-end or termination, and the 16 holidays need make-up days when they fall on days off.

Relying on US-style IP assignment. Under Copyright Act Art. 11 the employee is the author unless the contract names the employer, and the Patent Act implies 'appropriate remuneration' for service inventions unless the contract excludes it.
Terminating at the end of probation without notice or severance. Probation is not a statutory free-exit period.

Ignoring the 2025-26 changes: 16 holidays, day-based parental leave, hourly family care leave, sick-leave anti-retaliation, the workplace bullying chapter from 1 July 2026, and PDPA breach reporting to the PDPC.
semiconductorNotes: National core key technologies: the list (22 items in December 2023, 32 in December 2024, a 42-item expansion pre-announced November 2025 with an amended list published early 2026; verify) includes AI/HPC chip design, high-bandwidth chiplet interconnect design, heterogeneous integration packaging, ≤14nm process, GaN/SiC, chip security, cryogenic chips and qubits. A fabless design team can be in scope. Misappropriation for foreign or PRC use carries up to 12 years and NT$100M under the National Security Act, and companies themselves can be fined.

The TSMC 2nm case (indicted August 2025, convicted April 2026) shows the enforcement model. The leak was detected by internal monitoring, a supplier employee induced it, and the supplier entity was penalized NT$150M. Employers need clean-hire certifications, restrictions on bringing prior-employer data, and documented 'best efforts' prevention to avoid corporate liability (Trade Secrets Act Art. 13-4).

Trade secret program expectations: data classification, need-to-know access, DLP and logging disclosed in policy and the PDPA notice, NDAs, periodic training, and exit forensics with a written return certification. Without 'reasonable protective measures', information may not qualify as a trade secret at all.

PRC-related risk: MJIB has run 100+ poaching investigations since 2020 (11 firms and 90 people questioned in March 2025; 17 firms and 114 people in July-August 2026). Vet recruiters, contractors and JV partners for concealed PRC ownership. Staff on government-commissioned or subsidized core key technology projects need approval to travel to mainland China, continuing after they leave (Cross-Strait Act Art. 9; fines NT$2M-10M). Adopt a PRC travel and device policy for everyone.

Talent market: engineers compare offers against TSMC and MediaTek cash profit-sharing and bonuses worth many months of base pay, paid quarterly or annually. A Taiwan subsidiary must state an employee-compensation percentage of profit in its articles (Company Act Art. 235-1). Taiwan-listed rivals must also earmark part of it for rank-and-file staff under the 2024 Securities and Exchange Act amendment (verify details). US RSUs and overtime-inclusive pay modeling are key differentiators.

Non-competes are enforced by Taiwan courts only when they meet Art. 9-1 (paid, at most 2 years, narrow). For key engineers moving to competitors, combine a compliant paid restraint with trade-secret and national-security reminders rather than relying on US-style unpaid covenants.

Lab, test or fab operations raise the site to high OSH risk (electronic component manufacturing): hazardous-chemical controls, special health checks, maternal-health protections, and no 10pm-6am work for pregnant or breastfeeding employees. General night work by women no longer needs union consent after Judicial Yuan Interpretation No. 807 (2021), but safety and transport measures are still expected.

Export controls: check US EAR deemed-export rules for foreign-national staff with access to controlled technology, and Taiwan's strategic high-tech commodities (SHTC) controls, which have reportedly added major PRC chip entities (verify current ITA lists) before sharing technology with third parties.
